readMeFirst: PIN-FAMILIES.md, beside this file. A row is one repair CANDIDATE against one disappearance SHAPE of one PROPERTY. status is measured-retained | measured-not-retained | unmeasured | not-repairable-in-compiler, and a measured-* status is only allowed where lib/pin-families.mjs can recompute the number from data/ and test/pin-families.test.mjs does. A number that no test recomputes is not evidence here, so a one-off lab run rides along as labObservation or intervention and never as a status. How many rows this table holds, and which of them are recomputed rather than typed in by a human, is counted by tableCensus() in lib/pin-families.mjs and stated in the "Which rows are recomputed, and which a human typed" section of PIN-FAMILIES.md -- do not count the rows by eye.

wipe-pin/volatile-memset.what: WipePin makes the zero-fill llvm.memset in the named function volatile, at the start of the LLVM optimisation pipeline

wipe-pin-gcc/volatile-asm-barrier.what: WipePinGcc puts a volatile asm barrier around the zero-fill __builtin_memset in the named function
wipe-pin-gcc/volatile-asm-barrier.position: GIMPLE, directly after cfg, before ssa/einline/dse1

wipe-pin/pin-the-helper-by-name.what: the same pin, asked for the helper the target calls rather than for the target
wipe-pin/pin-the-helper-by-name.position: pipeline start, on IR, in whichever unit defines the helper

pass-delete/attributed-position.what: delete the pass the loss is attributed to (and separately the pass after it) from the pipeline string the compiler itself printed, and replay under opt and llc
pass-delete/attributed-position.position: the attributed leaf of clang's own -print-pipeline-passes string

gcc/fdisable-tree-pass.what: take the GIMPLE pass out of gcc's pipeline with -fdisable-tree-<pass> and rebuild, the same idea as the clang candidate through the only channel gcc offers
gcc/fdisable-tree-pass.position: the pass gcc's own -fdump-tree-all sequence names as the first dump at which the wipe stops making a difference

wipe-pin/asm-barrier-after-call.what: WipePin with WPIN_BARRIER_CALLS=1 puts an empty asm sideeffect, taking the destination and clobbering memory, directly after a plain zero-fill call of memset, __memset_chk or memset.<suffix> and after a plain call of bzero or bzero.<suffix>; the call itself is left as it is (compiler/schema/wipe-pin.md §14.4)
wipe-pin/asm-barrier-after-call.instrument: compiler/llvm-repair (WPIN_BARRIER_CALLS=1); measured only outside this tree, on a patched build per clang version
wipe-pin/asm-barrier-after-call.position: pipeline start, on IR, after the call

wipe-pin-gcc/asm-barrier-after-call.what: WipePinGcc with WPIN_BARRIER_CALLS=1 puts its volatile asm barrier directly after a zero-fill BUILT_IN_MEMSET_CHK and after a bzero call (compiler/schema/wipe-pin.md §14.4)
wipe-pin-gcc/asm-barrier-after-call.instrument: compiler/gcc-repair (WPIN_BARRIER_CALLS=1); measured only outside this tree, on a patched gcc-13 build
wipe-pin-gcc/asm-barrier-after-call.position: GIMPLE, directly after cfg, after the call

wipe-pin/zero-copy-to-volatile-memset.what: WipePin with WPIN_ZERO_COPY=1 replaces an llvm.memcpy from an all-zero constant global by a volatile llvm.memset of the same destination, length and alignment (form intrinsic), and puts the barrier of wipe-pin/asm-barrier-after-call after a plain memcpy, __memcpy_chk or memcpy.<suffix> call from one (form call) (compiler/schema/wipe-pin.md §14.5)
wipe-pin/zero-copy-to-volatile-memset.instrument: compiler/llvm-repair (WPIN_ZERO_COPY=1); measured only outside this tree, on a patched build per clang version

wipe-pin-gcc/asm-barrier-after-zero-copy.what: WipePinGcc with WPIN_ZERO_COPY=1 puts its volatile asm barrier after an aggregate copy, a BUILT_IN_MEMCPY or a memcpy / __memcpy_chk call whose source is an all-zero read-only static (compiler/schema/wipe-pin.md §14.5)
wipe-pin-gcc/asm-barrier-after-zero-copy.instrument: compiler/gcc-repair (WPIN_ZERO_COPY=1); measured only outside this tree, on a patched gcc-13 build
wipe-pin-gcc/asm-barrier-after-zero-copy.position: GIMPLE, directly after cfg, after the copy

pass-delete/every-dse-leaf.what: delete every dse leaf from the pipeline string clang printed (not only the attributed one) and replay under opt and llc
pass-delete/every-dse-leaf.instrument: a lab replay outside this tree (clang-18 18.1.3, opt-18, llc-18 -O2)
pass-delete/every-dse-leaf.position: every dse leaf of clang's own -print-pipeline-passes string

wipe-pin/buffer-barrier-at-lifetime-end.what: WipePin with WPIN_BUFFER_BARRIER=1 puts the empty asm sideeffect of wipe-pin/asm-barrier-after-call, taking the buffer, directly before each llvm.lifetime.end (with none, before each ret) of every stack buffer of a function in scope that a zero fill writes: a zero-fill memset or call, a copy from an all-zero constant, or a store of zero inside a loop into an array, struct or variable-length alloca (compiler/schema/wipe-pin.md §14.6; compiler/llvm-repair/README.md, The buffer barrier)
wipe-pin/buffer-barrier-at-lifetime-end.instrument: compiler/llvm-repair (WPIN_BUFFER_BARRIER=1); measured with this tree's build only by lab runs whose notes are outside this repository
wipe-pin/buffer-barrier-at-lifetime-end.position: pipeline start, on IR, at the end of the buffer's lifetime

wipe-pin-gcc/buffer-barrier-at-clobber.what: WipePinGcc with WPIN_BUFFER_BARRIER=1 puts its volatile asm barrier, taking &buf, directly before each end-of-scope clobber of every local buffer of a function in scope that a zero fill writes (with none, before each return): a zero-fill memset, __memset_chk or bzero, a copy from an all-zero read-only static, or a store of zero into an aggregate inside a loop (compiler/schema/wipe-pin.md §14.6; compiler/gcc-repair/README.md, The buffer barrier)
wipe-pin-gcc/buffer-barrier-at-clobber.instrument: compiler/gcc-repair (WPIN_BUFFER_BARRIER=1); measured with this tree's build only by lab runs whose notes are outside this repository
wipe-pin-gcc/buffer-barrier-at-clobber.position: GIMPLE, directly after cfg, before the buffer's end-of-scope clobber

labObservation.what: clang-18 18.1.3, x86-64: the pre-optimisation IR of each file through the pipeline clang printed with every dse leaf deleted, then llc-18 -O2. The wipe was still eliminated in 35 of 51 files of another corpus and in 70 of the 113 cells ../ai-generated/data/r2-build-rows.json reports eliminated at clang-18 -O2, and in all 35 and 70 the zero stores were in the IR handed to instruction selection and gone from the MIR after x86-isel. With every llvm.lifetime.end removed from that IR, 35/35 and 70/70 survived; removing llvm.lifetime.start, or turning stack colouring off, kept 0. Every eliminated file had its wipe directly before the buffer's lifetime end in the same basic block, and every surviving one had the end in another block or a call between (0 exceptions in 164). Naming the code that deletes the stores DAGCombiner::visitLIFETIME_END is an inference: read from upstream llvmorg-18.1.3 and matched to the measured properties, not observed in the build. These are counts of a replay with dse removed, not of a repair, and not of -O2 as written; an earlier reading of the same replay that gave 33/51 and 63/113 had misread nine pinpad files whose two listings differ only by a one-byte frame shift.

The two quotes say why every other candidate misses the shape: at pipeline start the loop is still a loop, so there is no memset to pin and no call to put a barrier after. The buffer barrier does not need one; it anchors at the end of the buffer's lifetime. It covers stack buffers of functions in scope only: a loop into an argument's memory, a global or the heap gets nothing, and a volatile store loop needs no repair in the first place. A barrier is not a pinned[] site and not an unhandled count; the record lists it in bufferBarriers. E3 v2 is 52 machine-made rewrites of generated files, each wipe rewritten as a loop of zero stores, written after the gap was seen, so the lab run shows the gap closed on those rewrites, not on loops a model wrote. Until 2026-11-09 this shape's only row was candidate none, not-repairable-in-compiler by construction (no site at the position either plugin runs); the buffer barrier landed that day and needs no such site, so that row was replaced by this one and the gcc one beside it.
